analysis:
All four units are documentation-only changes (docs/architecture/inference.md, docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md). No executable code, configuration or deployment surface changes in the supplied evidence.

The prefix-cache.md patch (hunks at lines 324 and 534-540) documents that wide prefill chunking (2,048-token plain chunks for dense Qwen3.5/3.8, GPT-OSS and Gemma 4, via EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift usesWidePrefillChunk) moves durable SSD checkpoint boundaries. The first retained boundary becomes 2,048 tokens, and the deepest boundary at or below a hint can sit up to 2,047 tokens below it. Security effect: SSD cache donations/hits become coarser for these models. This does not widen the T-041 at-rest surface. It does not change the HMAC lookup tags, the 30-minute TTL, salt scoping, or the KEK-based crypto purge. It slightly narrows what gets persisted and does not loosen the per-donation gate, so the SEC-035 accepted-risk posture is unchanged in kind.

The inference.md head excerpts (lines 1645-2268) are mostly unchanged context. The changed ranges in the supplied file_changes are the scheduler-config table (about lines 1087-1146) and the invariant 8/9 text (2028-2041). The table rows are outside the supplied text units and appear only in a truncated patch excerpt. Invariant 8 is only partially visible: it starts at line 2028 in unit 12 and continues in unit 13. It documents that the default prompt geometry never widens the largest schedulable chunk or a bidirectional media chunk, with media capped at 512 (bidirectionalMediaPrefillChunkCeiling). This is a documented control, not a regression.

Remaining integration questions: the actual code in EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift (prefillGeometry, usesWidePrefillChunk) and SchedulerV2 (prefillChunkCap) was not supplied. The docs' claims about wider chunks, memory admission and Gemma 4 ring bounds (invariant 9) cannot be verified here. I flag no vulnerability, and I treat the missing code as a coverage limit rather than evidence of safety. A reviewer of any companion code PR should confirm that wider chunks still respect GlobalKVCacheBudget and ProcessMemoryLedger admission (availability, T-029-adjacent) and Gemma 4's 2,048 ring limit.
